intent.raw_query: Japan family with kids, $4500, cherry blossom season 2026, 10 days from NYC

selected_hotel.name: Maruyama Park, Gion district, Kyoto Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience the iconic Japanese hanami (flower viewing) tradition under hundreds of blooming cherry trees. Maruyama Park in Kyoto is home to a famous weeping cherry tree illuminated at night. Bring a picnic blanket, enjoy local street food stalls, and join locals in celebrating the fleeting beauty of sakura season. Perfect for families with children who will love the festive atmosphere.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market, a paradise for food lovers and families alike. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), grilled scallops, matcha ice cream, and seasonal street snacks. Vendors are friendly and welcoming to children, making it an immersive and delicious cultural experience. A guided walking food tour adds historical context about Tokyo's culinary heritage.
experiences.location: Tsukiji Outer Market, Chuo City, Tokyo

experiences.name: Fushimi Inari Shrine Hike
experiences.description: Walk through thousands of iconic vermilion torii gates winding up the sacred Mount Inari. This UNESCO-recognized Shinto shrine dates back to 711 AD and offers a deeply spiritual and visually stunning experience. Families can hike as far as they like — the lower trails are manageable for children — while learning about Japanese religious traditions and fox deity folklore from informational plaques along the path.
experiences.location: Fushimi Inari Taisha, Fushimi Ward, Kyoto

experiences.name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park
experiences.description: A profoundly moving and educational experience for families, the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum chronicles the events of August 6, 1945, and promotes a message of global peace. Walk through the Peace Memorial Park, see the iconic A-Bomb Dome, and fold paper cranes at the Children's Peace Monument. The museum is thoughtfully curated to be accessible and impactful for visitors of all ages, offering a vital historical and cultural lesson.
experiences.location: Peace Memorial Park, Naka Ward, Hiroshima

experiences.name: Ninja and Samurai Experience Workshop
experiences.description: Immerse the whole family in Japan's legendary warrior culture with a hands-on ninja and samurai workshop. Children and adults alike can dress in authentic costumes, learn basic sword techniques, practice shuriken (throwing star) throwing, and receive a certificate of completion. Knowledgeable instructors share the history of the samurai code Bushido and ninja espionage traditions, blending entertainment with genuine cultural education in a fun, safe environment.
experiences.location: Samurai and Ninja Museum, Gion district, Kyoto

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Japan
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Maruyama Park, Gion district, Kyoto Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and settle in after landing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Kansai International Airport at 13:00. Take the Haruka Express train to Kyoto Station (approx. 75 min, ~¥1,800 with IC card). Check in to your boutique stay in Maruyama Park, Gion district. Take a gentle stroll through Maruyama Park to see the famous weeping cherry blossom tree (Gion Shidare-zakura) — one of Kyoto's most iconic cherry blossom spots and free to enter.
day_by_day.evening: Walk through the atmospheric Gion district lantern-lit streets. Explore Hanamikoji Street for a glimpse of traditional machiya townhouses and possible geisha sightings. Visit Yasaka Shrine (free entry, open 24 hours) — beautifully lit in the evening.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or grab a quick bite at Kansai Airport convenience store (7-Eleven or Lawson, ~¥400–600)
meals.lunch: Ekiben (station bento box) from Kyoto Station food hall (~¥700–1,000)
meals.dinner: Ramen at a local Gion-area ramen shop such as Kyoto Ramen Koji on the 10th floor of Kyoto Station or a nearby noodle shop (~¥800–1,200)

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a Suica or ICOCA IC card at the airport for seamless transit throughout the trip. Convenience stores (konbini) are your best friend for cheap, quality snacks and meals. April 15 is peak cherry blossom season — Maruyama Park will likely be stunning.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Fushimi Inari Taisha (free entry) — the iconic shrine with thousands of vermillion torii gates. Go early (by 8:00 AM) to beat the crowds. Hike as far up the mountain trail as energy allows — even the first 30 minutes offers spectacular views and photo opportunities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to central Kyoto and visit Tofuku-ji Temple (¥500 entry for garden) — a historic Zen temple with beautiful moss gardens and cherry blossom trees along the Tsutenkyo Bridge walkway. Walk back toward Gion and explore Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka — preserved historic stone-paved lanes lined with traditional shops and cafes.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Maruyama Park for a hanami (cherry blossom viewing) evening picnic. Pick up bento boxes and snacks from a nearby konbini or Nishiki Market. The park is illuminated at night during cherry blossom season — a magical and free experience.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast (onigiri, tamagoyaki, coffee) near the hotel (~¥400–600)
meals.lunch: Inari sushi (kitsune-zushi) near Fushimi Inari — a local specialty, sold at stalls near the shrine (~¥500–800)
meals.dinner: Picnic bento from Lawson or 7-Eleven enjoyed in Maruyama Park under the cherry blossoms (~¥700–1,000)

day_by_day.notes: Fushimi Inari is free and one of Japan's most visited sites — arrive early. Wear comfortable walking shoes as you'll cover 6–10 km today. Nishiki Market (Kyoto's 'Kitchen') is great for free tastings and cheap street food snacks.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion) — entry ¥500. One of Japan's most iconic landmarks, reflecting beautifully in the surrounding pond. Arrive early to avoid crowds. Afterward, walk to nearby Ryoan-ji Temple (¥600) to see Japan's most famous Zen rock garden — a meditative and culturally rich experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Nishiki Market (free to walk through) for street food snacks and local produce. Then explore Kyoto Imperial Palace Park (free) — a large, open green space with historical palace grounds. The park is perfect for families and offers free guided tours of the palace interior (book in advance at the Imperial Household Agency).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Pontocho Alley — a narrow lantern-lit dining street running parallel to the Kamo River. Enjoy dinner at one of the more affordable restaurants here. Afterward, stroll along the Kamo River banks where locals gather in the evenings.

meals.breakfast: Morning set at a local kissaten (Japanese coffee shop) near Gion (~¥500–700)
meals.lunch: Street food from Nishiki Market — try yuba (tofu skin), grilled skewers, and tamagoyaki (~¥600–900 total)
meals.dinner: Affordable set meal (teishoku) at a Pontocho restaurant — look for lunch-style set menus offered at dinner (~¥1,000–1,500)

day_by_day.notes: Saturday will be busy at top attractions — arrive at Kinkaku-ji by 9:00 AM. Kyoto Imperial Palace tours are free but require advance registration at the Imperial Household Agency website. Pontocho has options across all budgets — look for places with plastic food displays and set menus posted outside.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nara (45 min from Kyoto by Kintetsu train, ~¥720 one way). Visit Nara Park (free) and interact with the famous free-roaming deer — a wonderful family activity. Feed them shika senbei (deer crackers, ¥200/pack sold at the park).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Todai-ji Temple (¥600) — home to Japan's largest bronze Buddha statue, an awe-inspiring cultural and historical landmark. Explore Kasuga Taisha Shrine (free outer grounds) with its hundreds of stone and bronze lanterns lining the forested pathways.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto by early evening. Relax and explore the streets around your hotel in Gion. Visit Chion-in Temple (free outer grounds, one of Japan's largest temple gates) just a short walk from Maruyama Park.

meals.breakfast: Konbini breakfast before catching the train (~¥400–600)
meals.lunch: Kakinoha-zushi (persimmon leaf sushi) — a Nara specialty available at shops near Todai-ji (~¥800–1,200)
meals.dinner: Gyudon (beef rice bowl) at Yoshinoya or Sukiya near Kyoto Station (~¥500–700)

day_by_day.notes: Nara is extremely family-friendly — children love the deer. The deer can be pushy around food, so supervise young children. A Kintetsu Day Pass (~¥1,500) may be cost-effective if you plan multiple Kintetsu rides. Return to Kyoto by 17:00 to avoid rush hour crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Arashiyama district (30 min from Gion by bus or train). Visit the iconic Arashiyama Bamboo Grove (free) — walk through towering bamboo stalks for a surreal, unforgettable experience. Go early (before 9:00 AM) for the best light and fewer crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Tenryu-ji Temple and its UNESCO-listed garden (¥500 for garden, ¥800 to enter temple buildings) — a stunning Zen garden with cherry blossoms framing the mountain backdrop. Walk along the Oi River and Togetsu-kyo Bridge — a beautiful, free scenic area. Explore the charming Arashiyama shopping street for affordable souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Gion area. Visit the Gion Corner cultural theater (¥3,150 per person) for a 50-minute showcase of traditional Japanese arts including tea ceremony, ikebana, koto music, and maiko dance — excellent cultural value for families.

meals.breakfast: Onigiri and green tea from konbini (~¥400)
meals.lunch: Yudofu (tofu hot pot) set lunch in Arashiyama — several affordable restaurants near Tenryu-ji offer lunch sets (~¥1,000–1,400)
meals.dinner: Conveyor belt sushi (kaiten-zushi) near Kyoto Station or Gion — budget ~¥100–150 per plate, total ~¥1,000–1,500

day_by_day.notes: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove is free but extremely crowded by mid-morning. The Gion Corner show is optional but highly recommended for families interested in Japanese culture — book tickets in advance online. Bus Day Pass (¥700) is excellent value for Arashiyama day trips.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to Osaka (15 min from Kyoto by shinkansen or 30 min by regular Hankyu/JR train, ~¥560 by JR). Visit Osaka Castle (castle tower entry ¥600, grounds free) — a magnificent 16th-century fortress surrounded by cherry blossom trees and a large park, perfect for families and history enthusiasts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Dotonbori — Osaka's vibrant entertainment and food district. Walk along the canal, see the famous Glico Running Man sign, and explore the lively street food scene. Visit Kuromon Ichiba Market (free to walk through) — Osaka's famous food market with fresh seafood, street snacks, and local produce.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Osaka's famous street food culture in Dotonbori for dinner. Explore Shinsaibashi shopping arcade (free, covered arcade) for budget souvenir shopping before returning to Kyoto.

meals.breakfast: Konbini or hotel area café (~¥400–600)
meals.lunch: Osaka street food in Dotonbori — try takoyaki (octopus balls, ~¥500), kushikatsu (fried skewers, ~¥100–150 each), and okonomiyaki (~¥800–1,000 total)
meals.dinner: Ramen or udon at a local Dotonbori restaurant (~¥800–1,200)

day_by_day.notes: Osaka is a must-visit food city — budget extra for street food. The JR Kyoto–Osaka route is the most budget-friendly option. Dotonbori is lively and family-friendly in the evening. Keep an eye on children in crowded areas.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Kiyomizu-dera Temple (¥400 entry) — one of Japan's most celebrated temples, perched on a wooden stage overlooking Kyoto with panoramic views and cherry blossoms. Explore the surrounding Higashiyama district — a beautifully preserved historic neighborhood with traditional shops and teahouses.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the Philosopher's Path (Tetsugaku-no-Michi) — a 2 km stone path along a canal lined with hundreds of cherry trees. A free, peaceful, and scenic walk beloved by locals and visitors alike. Stop at Nanzen-ji Temple (free outer grounds, ¥600 for sub-temples) — a grand Zen temple complex with a massive sanmon gate.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Gion for a farewell stroll through the neighborhood. Visit Kennin-ji Temple (¥600) — Kyoto's oldest Zen temple, which stays open until 17:30. Enjoy a quiet evening dinner near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Japanese breakfast set at a local café near Gion (~¥600–900)
meals.lunch: Matcha soft serve and light snacks along Higashiyama shopping street (~¥500–700)
meals.dinner: Tofu cuisine set meal (kaiseki-lite) at an affordable Kyoto restaurant near Maruyama Park (~¥1,200–1,800)

day_by_day.notes: Kiyomizu-dera is one of Japan's most iconic sites — arrive by 9:00 AM before tour groups arrive. The Philosopher's Path is at its most beautiful during cherry blossom season. Wear comfortable shoes as today involves significant uphill walking.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Hiroshima (take the Shinkansen from Kyoto, ~1.5 hours, ~¥5,700 one way — consider a JR Pass if not already purchased). Visit the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum (¥200) — a deeply moving and historically significant museum documenting the atomic bombing of 1945. Essential for history-focused travelers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Peace Memorial Park (free) — walk among the monuments, the Atomic Bomb Dome (UNESCO World Heritage Site), and the Children's Peace Monument. Take a short ferry to Miyajima Island (ferry ~¥180 each way) to see the famous floating torii gate of Itsukushima Shrine (¥300 entry) — a breathtaking cultural landmark.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hiroshima city for dinner before catching the Shinkansen back to Kyoto. Arrive back in Kyoto by 20:00–21:00.

meals.breakfast: Konbini breakfast before departing (~¥400–600)
meals.lunch: Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki — a local specialty distinct from Osaka style, layered with noodles (~¥900–1,200)
meals.dinner: Quick dinner at Hiroshima Station food court before the return Shinkansen (~¥800–1,200)

day_by_day.notes: Hiroshima is a profound and important historical destination. The Peace Museum is appropriate for older children and adults — be prepared for emotional content. A JR Pass (7-day or 14-day) makes Shinkansen travel much more economical if you plan multiple bullet train journeys. Miyajima Island also has free-roaming deer like Nara.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning — visit Heian Jingu Shrine (free outer grounds, ¥600 for garden) — a large, colorful Shinto shrine built in 1895 with a beautiful garden famous for its weeping cherry blossoms. A peaceful and culturally rich way to spend a final Kyoto morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Kyoto National Museum (¥700 general admission) near your hotel in the Gion area — houses an outstanding collection of Japanese art, ceramics, paintings, and historical artifacts spanning centuries. Then do final souvenir shopping at Nishiki Market or the Gion area shops.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a memorable final Kyoto dinner — try a mid-range kaiseki (Japanese multi-course meal) at a local restaurant, or enjoy a nicer sushi restaurant for a special farewell meal. Take a final evening stroll through Maruyama Park and Gion.

meals.breakfast: Konbini or local bakery near hotel (~¥400–600)
meals.lunch: Affordable bento or soba noodles near Heian Jingu (~¥700–1,000)
meals.dinner: Slightly elevated budget dinner — sushi restaurant or mid-range Japanese restaurant in Gion (~¥2,000–3,000 per person as a treat)

day_by_day.notes: Today is a good day to pick up omiyage (souvenir gifts) — Nishiki Market and Gion shops have great options. Pack bags tonight if departing tomorrow. Heian Jingu garden is particularly beautiful in cherry blossom season.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Kyoto — take a quiet sunrise walk through Maruyama Park one last time to soak in the cherry blossoms. Visit any remaining nearby sites you may have missed — Chion-in Temple gate (free) or Shoren-in Temple (¥500) are both within walking distance of the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of accommodation. Travel to Kansai International Airport via Kyoto Station — take the JR Haruka Express (~75 min, ~¥1,800). Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for check-in and security. Pick up last-minute airport souvenirs or duty-free items.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Kansai International Airport. Reflect on an incredible 10 days of cherry blossoms, history, culture, and unforgettable Japanese experiences.

meals.breakfast: Final Japanese breakfast — tamago gohan (egg on rice) or miso soup set at a local diner near the hotel (~¥500–800)
meals.lunch: Airport ramen or sushi at Kansai Airport food court (~¥1,000–1,500)
meals.dinner: On the plane or at the airport departure lounge

day_by_day.notes: Leave extra time for the airport journey on a Saturday — trains can be busy. Use remaining yen on airport food, duty-free, or exchange back to home currency (note: exchange rates at airport are less favorable). Ensure IC card is returned at the airport for a refund of the deposit (~¥500). Keep all receipts for tax-free shopping refunds at the airport.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Transfer — Flight LH lands at 13:00, so no morning activity. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and take the Narita/Haneda Express or airport limousine bus to central Tokyo or connect onward to Kyoto via Shinkansen. Estimated travel time to Kyoto: 2.5–3.5 hours depending on airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check-in at Boutique Stay in Maruyama Park, Gion district. After settling in, take a gentle stroll through Maruyama Park to see the famous weeping cherry tree (shidarezakura) in bloom — a perfect soft introduction to hanami culture. The park is steps from your hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Wander the stone-paved Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka lanes near Gion for a first taste of historic Kyoto. Browse small craft shops and soak in the lantern-lit atmosphere as dusk falls.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or airport convenience store snack (7-Eleven or Lawson at the airport offer onigiri, sandwiches, and hot drinks)
meals.lunch: Quick ramen or udon at a noodle shop inside Kyoto Station upon arrival — try Kyoto Ramen Koji on the 10th floor of the station building (¥900–¥1,400)
meals.dinner: Kaiseki-lite set meal at a local Gion restaurant such as Omen Gion (handmade udon, ¥1,200–¥1,800 per person) — a relaxed, family-friendly introduction to Kyoto cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag will be a factor. Prioritize hydration and an early bedtime. Purchase an IC card (Suica/ICOCA) at the airport for seamless transit throughout the trip. April 15 typically falls within peak cherry blossom season in Kyoto.

day_by_day.morning: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park (Featured Experience) — Begin the day with a classic hanami breakfast picnic under the iconic weeping cherry tree. Arrive by 8:00 AM before crowds gather. Pick up bento boxes, taiyaki, and matcha drinks from nearby Nishiki Market stalls or a convenience store the night before.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Chion-in Temple and Shoren-in Temple, both a short walk from Maruyama Park. Explore the massive sanmon gate at Chion-in and the serene camphor trees at Shoren-in. Continue to Heian Shrine (15-min taxi or bus) whose large garden is spectacular with cherry blossoms lining the pond.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the Gion district at dusk — the best time to spot maiko (apprentice geisha) heading to evening engagements along Hanamikoji Street. Enjoy the illuminated cherry blossoms in Maruyama Park (evening light-up events typically run until 21:30 during blossom season).

meals.breakfast: Picnic-style hanami breakfast — purchase bento, onigiri, and taiyaki from Nishiki Market or a convenience store (¥500–¥800 per person)
meals.lunch: Tofu cuisine lunch at Tousuiro near Heian Shrine — Kyoto is famous for its delicate tofu dishes (¥1,500–¥2,500 per person)
meals.dinner: Yakitori and skewers at a casual izakaya near Gion such as Torito Gion — lively, family-friendly atmosphere (¥1,500–¥2,500 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable shoes for temple walking. Maruyama Park evening illuminations are free to enter. Check the Kyoto City Tourism website for exact light-up hours. Keep a light jacket — April evenings in Kyoto can be cool (12–16°C).

day_by_day.morning: Fushimi Inari Shrine Hike (Featured Experience) — Take bus #南5 or the JR Nara Line from Tofukuji Station to Inari Station (15 min from Gion). Start the hike by 8:30 AM to beat tour groups. Walk through thousands of vermilion torii gates up sacred Mount Inari. The full loop takes 2–3 hours; families with young children can turn back at Yotsutsuji intersection (45 min up) for panoramic city views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to central Kyoto and visit Nishiki Market — Kyoto's famous covered shopping street nicknamed 'Kyoto's Kitchen.' Sample pickled vegetables, fresh mochi, grilled skewers, and matcha soft-serve. Then explore Nijo Castle (UNESCO World Heritage Site) with its famous 'nightingale floors' that squeak to detect intruders — a huge hit with children.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in Gion. Visit Yasaka Shrine (adjacent to Maruyama Park, free entry, open 24 hours) beautifully lit at night. Wind down with a matcha parfait at Gion Tsujiri, a celebrated Kyoto tea house.

meals.breakfast: Morning set at a local kissaten (Japanese coffee shop) near the hotel — toast, egg, and coffee (¥600–¥900)
meals.lunch: Street food lunch at Nishiki Market — graze on skewers, tofu donuts, and tamago (egg on a stick) for approximately ¥1,000–¥1,500 per person
meals.dinner: Shabu-shabu or sukiyaki at Mishima-tei near Nijo Castle — a mid-range hot pot experience perfect for families (¥2,500–¥4,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Fushimi Inari is free to enter and open 24/7. Wear sturdy shoes for the hike — the stone path can be uneven. Nijo Castle charges ¥1,030 per adult; children under 15 are free or discounted. Saturday crowds can be heavy at Nishiki Market — go before noon.

day_by_day.morning: Ninja and Samurai Experience Workshop (Featured Experience) — Book a morning session at Samurai Kembu Theater or Kyoto Samurai & Ninja Museum in central Kyoto (20-min taxi from Gion). Children and adults don costumes, learn sword techniques, and try shuriken (ninja star) throwing. Sessions typically run 60–90 minutes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion) — one of Japan's most iconic sights, the gold-leaf-covered Zen temple reflecting in its mirror pond is stunning during spring. Then head to Ryoan-ji Temple to contemplate its famous rock garden, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Both temples are in northwest Kyoto (accessible by bus from the city center).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Gion for a traditional Japanese public bath (sento) experience at Funaoka Onsen in Kita ward or a closer neighborhood bathhouse — a wonderful family wind-down ritual. Afterward, enjoy a quiet dinner near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Japanese breakfast set at the hotel or nearby café — miso soup, rice, grilled fish, pickles (¥800–¥1,200)
meals.lunch: Shokado bento box lunch at a restaurant near Kinkaku-ji — elegant lacquered box meals in the Kyoto tradition (¥1,500–¥2,500)
meals.dinner: Casual okonomiyaki (savory pancake) dinner at a teppanyaki restaurant in Gion — fun and interactive for families (¥1,200–¥2,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Ninja/Samurai workshop in advance online — weekend slots fill quickly. Kinkaku-ji admission is ¥500 per person; Ryoan-ji is ¥600. The northwest Kyoto temples are best reached by Kyoto City Bus (¥230 flat fare with IC card). Funaoka Onsen is a historic bathhouse (¥500 entry) with a beautiful mosaic tile interior.

day_by_day.morning: Day Trip to Nara — Take the JR Miyakoji Rapid from Kyoto Station (45 min, ¥720). Visit Todai-ji Temple, home to Japan's largest bronze Buddha statue. Walk through Nara Park and hand-feed the famous free-roaming sika deer (shika sembei deer crackers sold nearby for ¥200) — an unforgettable family experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kasuga Taisha Shrine, a UNESCO-listed Shinto shrine with thousands of bronze and stone lanterns lining its forested approach. Stroll through the Naramachi merchant district with its traditional machiya townhouses, small museums, and craft shops.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto by early evening (last comfortable train around 18:30). Enjoy a relaxed dinner in the Pontocho alley — a narrow lantern-lit dining street parallel to the Kamo River with restaurants ranging from casual to upscale, many with riverside terrace seating (kawayuka) in spring.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or hotel breakfast before departure (¥400–¥700)
meals.lunch: Kakinoha-zushi (persimmon leaf-wrapped sushi) — Nara's signature dish — at Hiraso near Kintetsu Nara Station (¥1,200–¥1,800)
meals.dinner: Riverside terrace dining on Pontocho — try Pontocho Yoshikawa for tempura or Kichi Kichi Omurice for theatrical omelette rice (¥2,000–¥3,500 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Deer in Nara Park can be assertive — teach children to bow to the deer (they bow back!) and hold bags away from them. Todai-ji admission is ¥600 per adult. Nara is very walkable; a bicycle rental (¥1,000/day) is a fun family option. April weather in Nara is mild and pleasant.

day_by_day.morning: Arashiyama District — Take the JR Sagano Line or Randen tram from central Kyoto (30 min). Walk through the Arashiyama Bamboo Grove early morning (before 9 AM) for a magical, relatively crowd-free experience. Visit Tenryu-ji Temple and its UNESCO-listed Zen garden with cherry blossoms and a backdrop of forested mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Sagano Scenic Railway (Torokko Train) — a beloved family activity winding through the Hozu River gorge with stunning spring foliage (book tickets in advance, ¥880 each way). After the train, rent a rowboat on the Oi River or stroll the Togetsukyo Bridge area lined with cherry trees.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Kimono Forest at Arashiyama Station — 600 illuminated kimono fabric poles create a magical tunnel of light after dark. Return to Gion for dinner and a well-earned rest.

meals.breakfast: Yudofu (hot tofu) breakfast at Sagano Yudofu near Tenryu-ji — a quintessential Arashiyama tradition (¥1,200–¥1,800)
meals.lunch: Matcha soba noodles at a riverside restaurant in Arashiyama — light and refreshing (¥1,000–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Conveyor belt sushi (kaiten-zushi) at Musashi Sushi near Kyoto Station or central Kyoto — fun, affordable, and great for families (¥1,000–¥2,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Sagano Torokko Train well in advance — it sells out weeks ahead during cherry blossom season. Tenryu-ji admission is ¥500 (garden only) or ¥800 (including temple buildings). The Bamboo Grove is free. Arashiyama is very popular — arriving before 8:30 AM makes a significant difference in crowd levels.

day_by_day.morning: Travel Day: Kyoto → Hiroshima via Shinkansen — Check out of Kyoto hotel and take the Nozomi or Sakura Shinkansen from Kyoto Station to Hiroshima (1 hour 40 min, ¥10,580 with JR Pass or standard fare). Check into a mid-range hotel in central Hiroshima (e.g., Rihga Royal Hotel Hiroshima or Hotel Granvia Hiroshima).
day_by_day.afternoon: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park (Featured Experience) — Walk from the hotel (or take a tram) to the Peace Memorial Park. Begin at the A-Bomb Dome (Genbaku Dome), the haunting UNESCO-listed skeletal ruins preserved as a monument. Enter the Peace Memorial Museum — allow 2 hours for a thorough, age-appropriate visit. The museum chronicles the atomic bombing with powerful artifacts, testimonies, and a message of global peace.
day_by_day.evening: Reflect and decompress with a peaceful evening walk through the Peace Memorial Park. Light a paper lantern on the Motoyasu River if lantern floating events are scheduled (check local listings). Enjoy dinner in the Nagarekawa entertainment district.

meals.breakfast: Shinkansen ekiben (station bento box) purchased at Kyoto Station — a beloved Japanese travel tradition (¥1,000–¥1,500)
meals.lunch: Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki at Okonomimura (Okonomiyaki Village) — a multi-floor building with dozens of stalls, each with a slightly different recipe (¥1,000–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Oyster cuisine at a local izakaya — Hiroshima produces 60% of Japan's oysters; try grilled, fried, or raw preparations at Kakifune Kanawa, a floating oyster restaurant on the river (¥2,000–¥3,500)

day_by_day.notes: The Peace Memorial Museum (¥200 per adult, children free) is a deeply moving experience — prepare children aged 8+ thoughtfully beforehand. The museum has English audio guides and exhibits. The A-Bomb Dome is free to view. Hiroshima's tram system is easy and cheap (¥180 flat fare) for getting around the city.

day_by_day.morning: Day Trip to Miyajima Island — Take the JR San'yo Line to Miyajimaguchi Station (30 min) then a 10-min JR ferry to Miyajima Island (covered by JR Pass). See the iconic floating torii gate of Itsukushima Shrine — one of Japan's most photographed sights. Visit the shrine complex (¥300 per adult) and explore the island's friendly deer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike or take the ropeway up Mount Misen for panoramic views of the Seto Inland Sea and surrounding islands. The summit area has walking trails and a small temple complex. Return to the shore and explore Omotesando shopping street for maple leaf manju (momiji manju) — the island's famous red bean-filled pastry — and local oyster snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hiroshima by late afternoon. Enjoy a final Hiroshima evening with a stroll along the Hondori covered shopping arcade and dinner in the city center.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast buffet (¥1,200–¥1,800) or convenience store near hotel
meals.lunch: Freshly grilled oysters and Miyajima oyster rice at a waterfront stall on the island (¥1,200–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Hiroshima-style ramen or tsukemen (dipping noodles) at a local ramen shop in central Hiroshima (¥900–¥1,400)

day_by_day.notes: The floating torii gate is best photographed at high tide when it appears to float — check tide tables in advance. The Miyajima Ropeway costs ¥1,840 round trip per adult. Momiji manju (¥100–¥150 each) make excellent souvenirs. The JR ferry to Miyajima is covered by JR Pass — a great saving.

day_by_day.morning: Travel Day: Hiroshima → Tokyo via Shinkansen — Check out of Hiroshima hotel and take the Nozomi Shinkansen to Tokyo (4 hours, ¥18,040 or JR Pass). Enjoy the ride — on a clear day, Mount Fuji is visible from the right side of the train around Shin-Fuji Station. Check into a mid-range Tokyo hotel (e.g., Shinjuku or Asakusa area recommended for culture and family activities).
day_by_day.afternoon: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour (Featured Experience) — Head to Tsukiji (accessible by Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line to Tsukiji Station). Explore the lively outdoor market with stalls selling fresh seafood, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), street snacks, and Japanese knives. Sample freely — this is Tokyo's premier food-lover destination and a vibrant family experience.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the nearby Hamarikyu Gardens (¥300 per adult) — a traditional Japanese garden with a tidal pond, cherry trees, and a historic teahouse. The contrast of the serene garden against the Tokyo skyline is striking. Return to the hotel area for dinner in the neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Ekiben bento from Hiroshima Station — buy before boarding (¥1,000–¥1,500)
meals.lunch: Tsukiji Market grazing lunch — fresh tuna sashimi, grilled scallops, tamagoyaki, and green tea ice cream from various stalls (¥1,500–¥2,500 per person)
meals.dinner: Tonkatsu (breaded pork cutlet) dinner at Maisen Aoyama or a local tonkatsu restaurant near the hotel — a Tokyo classic (¥1,500–¥2,500)

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is open daily (most stalls from 5 AM–2 PM) — arriving between 10 AM and noon is ideal for families. The Inner Market (Toyosu) requires advance booking for tuna auctions. Keep an eye on bags in crowded market areas. Hamarikyu Gardens closes at 17:00.

day_by_day.morning: Asakusa Cultural Morning — Visit Senso-ji Temple, Tokyo's oldest and most famous Buddhist temple, and walk the Nakamise shopping street lined with traditional craft stalls (open from 10 AM). Try ningyo-yaki (doll-shaped cakes), kaminari-okoshi (rice puff candy), and browse for omiyage (souvenirs). The temple grounds are free; the atmosphere is festive and family-friendly.
day_by_day.afternoon: Tokyo Skytree (adjacent to Asakusa) — take the elevator to the Tembo Deck at 350m for sweeping views over Tokyo, and on clear days, Mount Fuji. Then head to Akihabara Electric Town (10-min subway ride) for a fun family browse through multi-floor electronics stores, anime merchandise, and retro gaming arcades — a uniquely Tokyo experience.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening celebration dinner in Shinjuku or near the hotel. Visit the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck (free, open until 22:30 on most nights) for a spectacular free nighttime panorama of the city. End with dessert at a depachika (department store basement food hall) — a final taste of Japan's extraordinary food culture.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Japanese breakfast at the hotel or a neighborhood kissaten — miso soup, rice, tamagoyaki, and natto (¥800–¥1,200)
meals.lunch: Tempura lunch at a mid-range tempura restaurant in Asakusa such as Daikokuya Tempura (est. 1887) — crispy, light, and quintessentially Tokyo (¥1,500–¥2,500)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a teppanyaki restaurant in Shinjuku — chefs cook wagyu beef, seafood, and vegetables on an iron griddle tableside (¥3,000–¥5,000 per person for a special send-off)

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is free and open 24/7 though the Nakamise shops open at 10 AM. Tokyo Skytree admission is ¥2,100 (Tembo Deck) per adult — book online to avoid queues. Akihabara is best explored in the afternoon when all floors are open. The Tokyo Metropolitan Government observation deck is free and a fantastic budget-friendly alternative to paid observation decks. Pack purchases carefully — Japan's strict customs rules apply on departure.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Japan Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Maruyama Park, Gion district, Kyoto Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience the iconic Japanese hanami (flower viewing) tradition under hundreds of blooming cherry trees. Maruyama Park in Kyoto is home to a famous weeping cherry tree illuminated at night. Bring a picnic blanket, enjoy local street food stalls, and join locals in celebrating the fleeting beauty of sakura season. Perfect for families with children who will love the festive atmosphere.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market, a paradise for food lovers and families alike. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), grilled scallops, matcha ice cream, and seasonal street snacks. Vendors are friendly and welcoming to children, making it an immersive and delicious cultural experience. A guided walking food tour adds historical context about Tokyo's culinary heritage.
experiences.location: Tsukiji Outer Market, Chuo City, Tokyo

experiences.name: Fushimi Inari Shrine Hike
experiences.description: Walk through thousands of iconic vermilion torii gates winding up the sacred Mount Inari. This UNESCO-recognized Shinto shrine dates back to 711 AD and offers a deeply spiritual and visually stunning experience. Families can hike as far as they like — the lower trails are manageable for children — while learning about Japanese religious traditions and fox deity folklore from informational plaques along the path.
experiences.location: Fushimi Inari Taisha, Fushimi Ward, Kyoto

experiences.name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park
experiences.description: A profoundly moving and educational experience for families, the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum chronicles the events of August 6, 1945, and promotes a message of global peace. Walk through the Peace Memorial Park, see the iconic A-Bomb Dome, and fold paper cranes at the Children's Peace Monument. The museum is thoughtfully curated to be accessible and impactful for visitors of all ages, offering a vital historical and cultural lesson.
experiences.location: Peace Memorial Park, Naka Ward, Hiroshima

experiences.name: Ninja and Samurai Experience Workshop
experiences.description: Immerse the whole family in Japan's legendary warrior culture with a hands-on ninja and samurai workshop. Children and adults alike can dress in authentic costumes, learn basic sword techniques, practice shuriken (throwing star) throwing, and receive a certificate of completion. Knowledgeable instructors share the history of the samurai code Bushido and ninja espionage traditions, blending entertainment with genuine cultural education in a fun, safe environment.
experiences.location: Samurai and Ninja Museum, Gion district, Kyoto

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Transfer — Flight LH lands at 13:00. No morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer (pre-arranged limousine or Shinkansen Green Car from airport) to the boutique stay in Maruyama Park, Gion district, Kyoto.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hotel Check-In & Gion Orientation Stroll — Settle into the boutique property, freshen up, and take a leisurely self-guided walk through the atmospheric Gion district. Admire traditional machiya townhouses, spot maiko apprentice geisha, and soak in the historic ambiance of Hanamikoji Street.
day_by_day.evening: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park — Steps from the hotel, experience the iconic hanami (flower viewing) tradition under the famous weeping cherry tree (shidarezakura) beautifully illuminated at night. Enjoy the festive lantern-lit atmosphere unique to this park.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a meal on the flight or at the airport upon arrival — no breakfast scheduled at hotel.
meals.lunch: Light bento or ramen at a quality spot near Kyoto Station during transfer stopover, such as Kyoto Ramen Koji on the 10th floor of Kyoto Station Building.
meals.dinner: Kikunoi Honten — A three-Michelin-starred kaiseki restaurant in the Higashiyama district, just minutes from the hotel. Seasonal tasting menu showcasing spring ingredients and Kyoto's refined culinary heritage. Advance reservation essential.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. April 15 is typically peak cherry blossom season in Kyoto — Maruyama Park will be at or near full bloom. Keep the first evening relaxed to recover from jet lag. Confirm Kikunoi reservation months ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Fushimi Inari Shrine Hike — Depart early (by 7:30 AM) to beat crowds at this UNESCO-associated sacred site. Walk through thousands of vermilion torii gates winding up Mount Inari, enjoying misty morning light filtering through the tunnel of gates. Hire a private guide for cultural and historical context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Nishiki Market & Pontocho Exploration — Return to central Kyoto and explore Nishiki Market ('Kyoto's Kitchen'), sampling seasonal pickles, tofu, and street food. Stroll along the intimate Pontocho alley, one of Kyoto's most storied dining lanes, browsing restaurant menus for the evening.
day_by_day.evening: Ninja and Samurai Experience Workshop — Book a private family session at a premium cultural experience studio in Kyoto, where expert instructors guide the family through authentic ninja techniques, shuriken throwing, and samurai sword etiquette in traditional costume.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel premium Japanese breakfast — seasonal tofu, grilled fish, miso soup, and pickles prepared in traditional Kyoto style.
meals.lunch: Nishiki Market grazing lunch — sample fresh yudofu (tofu hot pot), tamagoyaki, and seasonal skewers from premium market vendors.
meals.dinner: Mizai — A Michelin-starred kaiseki restaurant in Pontocho with riverside seating. Exquisite spring tasting menu featuring bamboo shoots, sakura-themed dishes, and local Kyoto vegetables.

day_by_day.notes: Fushimi Inari is about 20 minutes by taxi from the hotel. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the hike — the full circuit takes 2–3 hours but partial routes are family-friendly. Book the Ninja & Samurai workshop as a private session for a more personalized experience.

day_by_day.morning: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion) & Ryoan-ji Zen Garden — Private guided tour of Kinkaku-ji, the breathtaking gold-leaf-covered temple reflected in Mirror Pond. Continue to Ryoan-ji to contemplate Japan's most famous rock garden — an ideal moment of mindfulness for the family.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove & Tenryu-ji — Travel to Arashiyama by private car. Walk through the ethereal bamboo grove, then explore Tenryu-ji, a UNESCO World Heritage Zen temple with a stunning garden. Optionally enjoy a private rickshaw (jinrikisha) ride through the scenic Saga-Arashiyama area.
day_by_day.evening: Traditional Tea Ceremony Experience — Attend a private, premium tea ceremony at an authentic Kyoto tea house near Gion, guided by a certified tea master. Learn the philosophy of wabi-sabi and practice the ritual of matcha preparation as a family.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel Japanese breakfast with seasonal additions — sakura mochi and spring vegetable dishes reflecting the April season.
meals.lunch: Shigetsu at Tenryu-ji — A renowned shojin ryori (Buddhist vegetarian cuisine) restaurant within the temple grounds, offering a serene garden view dining experience.
meals.dinner: Nakamura — One of Kyoto's oldest and most prestigious kaiseki restaurants (over 500 years of history), serving refined Kyoto cuisine in an elegant machiya setting.

day_by_day.notes: Saturdays in April are very busy at popular sites — depart for Kinkaku-ji by 8:00 AM for smaller crowds. A private guide is highly recommended for historical storytelling. Book the tea ceremony well in advance as premium private sessions fill quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Nijo Castle & Kyoto Imperial Palace — Private guided tour of Nijo Castle, a UNESCO World Heritage Site with its famous 'nightingale floors' and stunning Ninomaru Palace interiors. Continue to the Kyoto Imperial Palace and stroll the Imperial Park, which features beautiful cherry trees.
day_by_day.afternoon: Philosopher's Path & Nanzen-ji Temple — Walk the iconic Philosopher's Path (Tetsugaku-no-Michi), a canal-side stone path lined with hundreds of cherry trees in full bloom. Visit Nanzen-ji, a grand Zen temple complex with an impressive aqueduct and serene sub-temples.
day_by_day.evening: Gion Corner Cultural Show — Attend an exclusive performance at Gion Corner showcasing seven traditional Japanese art forms including maiko dance, koto music, ikebana flower arranging, and the tea ceremony. Afterward, stroll Hanamikoji Street hoping to glimpse geisha heading to evening engagements.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast with freshly prepared tamagoyaki, seasonal miso soup, and locally sourced Kyoto vegetables.
meals.lunch: Okutan Nanzen-ji — Japan's oldest tofu restaurant, serving refined yudofu (hot tofu) cuisine in a tranquil garden setting within the Nanzen-ji complex.
meals.dinner: Hyotei — A legendary three-Michelin-starred restaurant with over 450 years of history near Nanzen-ji, offering exquisite kaiseki with spring seasonal ingredients. One of Japan's most celebrated dining experiences.

day_by_day.notes: Nijo Castle requires advance timed-entry reservations. Hyotei requires reservations made several months in advance — this is one of Japan's most sought-after dining reservations. The Philosopher's Path is at its most spectacular during peak cherry blossom season.

day_by_day.morning: Day Trip to Nara — Private luxury transfer to Nara (45 minutes). Visit Todai-ji Temple, home to Japan's largest bronze Buddha statue. Walk through Nara Park, where over 1,200 freely roaming sacred deer delight families. Explore the Kasuga Grand Shrine with its thousands of stone and bronze lanterns.
day_by_day.afternoon: Nara Continued — Discover the quieter, less-visited Isuien Garden and Yoshikien Garden, two stunning traditional Japanese gardens near Todai-ji. Browse Naramachi, the preserved merchant district, for premium crafts and traditional shops.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto & Relaxation — Return to the hotel by private car. Enjoy a relaxing evening with an in-hotel or in-room kaiseki dinner, or unwind at a premium onsen (hot spring bath) if the boutique property offers one, or arrange a private session at a nearby sentō.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast — Japanese-style with seasonal accompaniments.
meals.lunch: Yoshikasuga — A refined restaurant near Nara Park serving traditional Yamato cuisine (ancient Nara-region cooking) with seasonal ingredients in an elegant setting.
meals.dinner: In-hotel private kaiseki dinner arranged by the concierge, or Kichisen — a legendary three-Michelin-starred kaiseki restaurant in Kyoto's Kinkaku-ji area (reservation required months in advance).

day_by_day.notes: Purchase shika senbei (deer crackers) for feeding the Nara deer — a highlight for families. Deer can be assertive; supervise young children closely. Isuien Garden charges a small admission fee and is far less crowded than main Nara attractions.

day_by_day.morning: Shinkansen to Hiroshima & Peace Memorial Museum — Depart Kyoto Station via Shinkansen (Nozomi, approx. 1 hour 45 min) to Hiroshima. Visit the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park — a profoundly moving and educational experience. Walk through the park, visit the Atomic Bomb Dome (Genbaku Dome), and fold origami cranes at the Children's Peace Monument.
day_by_day.afternoon: Miyajima Island (Itsukushima) — Take a short ferry to the sacred island of Miyajima. See the iconic floating torii gate of Itsukushima Shrine at high or mid-tide for maximum impact. Explore the island's shrines, pagodas, and encounter friendly deer. Hike or take the ropeway up Mount Misen for panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hiroshima & Overnight — Check into a premium Hiroshima hotel (e.g., Sheraton Grand Hiroshima or Hotel Granvia Hiroshima). Explore Hiroshima's lively Nagarekawa entertainment district in the evening.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel Kyoto breakfast before departure — early and light to allow time for the Shinkansen.
meals.lunch: Lunch on Miyajima Island — Kakiya, a renowned oyster restaurant on the island serving Hiroshima's famous grilled and raw oysters with mountain views.
meals.dinner: Kissui at Sheraton Grand Hiroshima — Elegant Japanese restaurant serving Hiroshima-style kaiseki and local specialties including oysters, momiji manju, and seasonal dishes.

day_by_day.notes: This is a powerful day emotionally, especially for families with children. The Peace Memorial Museum has age-appropriate sections; the experience is deeply educational. Check tide times for Miyajima's torii gate in advance. Overnight in Hiroshima to reduce travel fatigue.

day_by_day.morning: Hiroshima Castle & Shukkeien Garden — Visit Hiroshima Castle (reconstructed), exploring its museum of samurai armor, weapons, and regional history. Walk through Shukkeien, a beautifully landscaped traditional garden with a central pond, bridges, and spring cherry blossoms still lingering.
day_by_day.afternoon: Shinkansen to Tokyo — Depart Hiroshima via Nozomi Shinkansen (approx. 1.5 hours) to Tokyo. Private luxury transfer to the hotel (e.g., The Peninsula Tokyo, Aman Tokyo, or Park Hyatt Tokyo). Check in and settle into the new base.
day_by_day.evening: Shibuya & Roppongi Exploration — Experience Tokyo's electric energy with an evening visit to the Shibuya Crossing (world's busiest pedestrian intersection) and the Shibuya Sky observation deck for panoramic city views. Transfer to Roppongi for dinner.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel Hiroshima breakfast — Japanese or Western style at the hotel restaurant.
meals.lunch: Premium bento in Green Car on the Shinkansen — arrange a premium ekiben (station bento) from Hiroshima Station featuring local specialties.
meals.dinner: Ryugin — A three-Michelin-starred avant-garde Japanese cuisine restaurant in Roppongi, Tokyo. Chef Seiji Yamamoto's innovative interpretation of traditional Japanese cooking is a world-class experience.

day_by_day.notes: Hiroshima Castle's interior museum provides excellent context for Japan's feudal history. Book Tokyo luxury hotel well in advance for April — peak cherry blossom season drives high demand. Ryugin requires reservations months ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour — Explore the legendary Tsukiji Outer Market with a private guide. Sample freshly cut sushi, tamagoyaki, grilled seafood, and seasonal street food. Visit premium vendors for wagyu beef skewers, Hokkaido sea urchin, and artisan Japanese knives as souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: teamLab Planets or teamLab Borderless (Reopened 2024) & Odaiba — Visit the immersive digital art museum teamLab Planets in Toyosu for a breathtaking, family-friendly art experience. Explore the futuristic Odaiba waterfront with views of Tokyo Bay and a replica Statue of Liberty.
day_by_day.evening: Tokyo Tower & Shiba Park Cherry Blossoms — Visit Tokyo Tower at dusk for city views, and stroll Shiba Park where late-season cherry blossoms may still linger. Enjoy a refined dinner in the Minato district.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast at Tokyo luxury hotel — full Japanese or Western buffet with premium selections.
meals.lunch: Sushi Saito (if reservation secured — one of Japan's most exclusive sushi counters) or Sushi Yoshitake (three Michelin stars) near Ginza for an extraordinary omakase lunch experience.
meals.dinner: Azabu Yukimura — An intimate, critically acclaimed kaiseki restaurant in Azabu-Juban offering a deeply personal and seasonal tasting menu. Exceptional sake pairing available.

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is most vibrant in the morning — arrive by 8:00 AM. Sushi Saito is among the hardest reservations in the world — arrange through the hotel concierge. teamLab is extremely popular; pre-book timed entry tickets online.

day_by_day.morning: Senso-ji Temple & Asakusa Cultural District — Visit Tokyo's oldest and most iconic temple, Senso-ji, in the historic Asakusa district. Arrive early to experience the Nakamise shopping street before crowds build. Explore the traditional craft shops, purchase premium omamori charms, and admire the Kaminarimon Gate.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ueno Park & Tokyo National Museum — Stroll through Ueno Park, one of Tokyo's most famous hanami spots, where late cherry blossoms may still grace the pathways. Visit the Tokyo National Museum — Japan's oldest and largest museum — with an outstanding collection of samurai swords, imperial artifacts, Buddhist sculpture, and ukiyo-e woodblock prints.
day_by_day.evening: Akihabara & Harajuku Evening — Experience the vibrant contrasts of Tokyo: explore Akihabara's electronics and pop culture scene, then head to Harajuku's Takeshita Street for quirky fashion and crepes. End the evening in the upscale Omotesando boulevard for window shopping at flagship luxury stores.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel premium breakfast — enjoy the hotel's full spread before a full cultural day.
meals.lunch: Sometaro — A beloved traditional okonomiyaki (savory pancake) restaurant in Asakusa where you cook your own at the table — a fun, interactive family lunch experience.
meals.dinner: Sukiyabashi Jiro Honten (Ginza) — The legendary three-Michelin-starred sushi restaurant made world-famous by the documentary 'Jiro Dreams of Sushi.' An unmissable omakase experience for the serious food lover. Reservation through hotel concierge only.

day_by_day.notes: Sukiyabashi Jiro requires reservations made 1–2 months in advance through a hotel concierge — independent bookings are nearly impossible. The Tokyo National Museum's Gallery of Horyuji Treasures is a hidden gem. Ueno Park's cherry blossoms may be fading by April 23 but the atmosphere remains festive.

day_by_day.morning: Meiji Shrine & Harajuku Forest Walk — Begin the final morning with a serene walk through the forested path of Meiji Shrine, dedicated to Emperor Meiji and Empress Shoken. The towering torii gate and tranquil wooded approach offer a perfect contrast to Tokyo's urban energy. Participate in a traditional Shinto purification ritual.
day_by_day.afternoon: Shibuya Sky & Luxury Shopping in Ginza — Ascend Shibuya Sky for daytime 360° views of Tokyo in clear weather. Spend the final afternoon in Ginza — Tokyo's most prestigious shopping district — visiting flagship stores of Japanese luxury brands (Mikimoto pearls, Issey Miyake, Comme des Garçons) and department stores like Mitsukoshi for premium Japanese gifts and souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Kaiseki Dinner & Departure Preparation — Enjoy a memorable farewell dinner before returning to the hotel to pack and prepare for departure. Private luxury transfer to the airport arranged by the hotel concierge.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel final Japanese breakfast — a leisurely, reflective meal with premium seasonal selections.
meals.lunch: Ginza Kojyu — A Michelin three-starred kaiseki restaurant in Ginza offering an exquisite lunch tasting menu. Elegant, intimate, and perfect for a final luxury meal.
meals.dinner: Narisawa — Ranked among Asia's and the world's best restaurants, Chef Yoshihiro Narisawa's 'Innovative Satoyama Cuisine' bridges Japanese culinary tradition with nature-inspired creativity. A fitting, unforgettable farewell to Japan.

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Shrine is open from sunrise — arriving early ensures a peaceful experience before crowds. Narisawa requires reservations well in advance. Arrange departure airport transfer (private car to Narita or Haneda) at least 3 hours before flight. Purchase any remaining omiyage (gifts) at Mitsukoshi Ginza which has an exceptional basement food hall.
